author: praasz
title: Smart CI fails: GitHub API returns HTTP 500 on repos.get_branch call
signature: urllib error HTTPError HTTP Error 500 Internal Server Error|External Service

failed_jobs.name: Smart_CI
failed_jobs.symptom: Get affected components step fails with urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 500: Internal Server Error when calling gh_api.repos.get_branch

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check fails because Smart_CI job failed

key_errors:
File "/home/runner/work/openvino/openvino/./.github/actions/smart-ci/smart_ci.py", line 122, in get_changeset
    target_branch_head_commit = gh_api.repos.get_branch(target_branch).commit.sha
urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 500: Internal Server Error
====Error Body====
root_cause: The Smart CI script called the GitHub API endpoint repos.get_branch to determine the target branch head commit for changeset computation. GitHub's API returned an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error with an empty response body, indicating a transient server-side failure on GitHub's infrastructure. This caused the smart_ci.py script to raise an unhandled HTTPError and exit with code 1, blocking the entire merge-queue run. This is not related to any code change in the PR; it is a transient GitHub API availability issue.
reproduction_steps: N/A - transient GitHub API failure; not reproducible outside of the specific time window when GitHub's API was degraded.
recommended_actions: Re-trigger the merge-queue run (automated remediation requested via remediate_transient_failure).
If failures persist, check https://www.githubstatus.com/ for GitHub API degradation.
Consider adding retry logic with exponential backoff in smart_ci.py around the repos.get_branch API call to make the script resilient to transient GitHub API 5xx errors.
prevention_strategies: Add retry/backoff logic in smart_ci.py for GitHub API calls that are prone to transient 5xx errors. A simple exponential backoff with 3 retries would prevent this class of failure from blocking the merge queue.
historical_context: This is the first recorded occurrence of a GitHub API HTTP 500 error in Smart CI. Similar transient External Service failures in the Smart CI have been seen before (e.g., SSL certificate errors, ghapi/fastcore library issues). The fix pattern is always to re-trigger the run.
